**My reasoning, in my own words:**

I have been farming this land for fifty years. My plot is about 10.5 mu total. My son is in Baoding working construction. My back is not what it used to be, so I hire the machine crews that come through the village for ploughing, planting, and harvest. I pay them — it is worth it.

Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is what the land is for. I have done this my whole life. I will do it again. I plant wheat in October after the autumn harvest and corn in June right after the wheat comes off. Same land, same rotation my mother did.

For seeds, I buy from the village supply shop. They sell the improved wheat — the kind everyone uses now, 济麦 variety. For corn, I buy Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has this year. These give better yields than the old seeds.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea when the plants are growing. I do not calculate exactly — I buy a few bags and apply what feels right. My neighbor uses about the same.

Water is a worry. We pump from the well. It costs money. I irrigate wheat three times — once when I plant, once before it freezes, once at jointing. Corn I only water if the summer rain is not enough, maybe twice.

I also keep a small vegetable plot by the house — cabbage, garlic, beans — enough for myself and to give to neighbors. I do not sell it.

I will not try anything new this year. At my age, a bad harvest means real trouble. I follow what works.
